info.name: asyncdb
info.description:
The key journeys of the asyncdb HTTP/JSON API, in the order a client lives them: declare the table graph, write and read records, scan and page a range, delete a range, drop the table. Folders 1 to 7 run against one instance; folder 8 runs against the three of docker-compose.

Run the whole collection with the runner or with newman — the requests depend on the ones before them, and folder 0 makes a re-run start from a clean table.

Every assertion is drawn from doc/database, which is the spec: the codes are the documented codes, the statuses the documented statuses.

item.name: 4 · Keys the API must not mangle
item.description: A key is any non-empty string of at most 4 KiB, percent-encoded into the path. The path is split at its unencoded slashes before anything is decoded, so an encoded slash stays one segment.

item.name: 5 · Scans
item.description: Reading records in key order, which is what an ordered store is for. The range is a prefix, or a from that is inclusive and a to that is exclusive; reverse only changes the direction of travel; and a page that did not exhaust the range carries a cursor.

item.description: An operator action: one range tombstone instead of a delete per key. It takes the same range parameters as a scan, and refuses a request that names no range at all — deleting every record in a table is deleting the table.

item.name: 7 · Drop the tables
item.description: The cheap way to delete a lot of data: the column family goes and the data goes with it. A table that is not there is 404, and the records of a dropped table are gone even where the table is created again.

item.name: 8 · The cluster
item.description:
Only for the three instances of docker-compose, addressed by node1, node2 and node3. Every node answers for every key: a table is created on all of them, a record is served by the node that owns its key whichever node was asked, and a scan is asked of every node and merged back into key order.

Running this folder against a single instance fails at the first request, which is the point — it is asserting that there is a cluster.
